intro: Jeremiah is called the weeping prophet. He warned Judah for forty years that Babylon was coming, and lived to see Jerusalem fall.
Chapters one to twenty-five are his warnings, and his own painful prayers. Chapters twenty-six to forty-five tell his story: threats, prison, a muddy cistern, and the fall of the city.
Chapters forty-six to fifty-two speak to the nations, ending with the fall of Jerusalem retold.
Tradition holds that Jeremiah wrote it, with his scribe Baruch.
Listen for hope in the hardest times: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, and the promise of a new covenant.
